title: System Explorer collector declaration
description: A collector's static account of what it serves and what it means (DESIGN 19). Same on every host; instance binding is fleet configuration, never declared here. Members and meanings are binding, and every object is closed: six artefacts are generated from this file, so a misspelt member that validates is a sandbox path not granted or a redaction not performed, silently.

authority.description: What the deployment must grant. Generated into unit configuration; the collator never reads or passes any of it.

probe.description: Prose: what the probe verb establishes.

lookups.description: The collector's lookup palette: every parameterised read-only question its `lookup` verb answers (DESIGN 18). Collector-level, not per-collection, because a lookup name is the collector's own vocabulary — `route-get`, `resolve`, `snapshots-of` — and the palette doubles as usage documentation: question, expected input and a worked example are how a UI and an agent alike learn what can be asked. Bounds ride each entry exactly as the per-collection verbs member carries them: single-flight, and a response that hits its bound says so on the payload.

question.description: The question this collection answers, in the words someone would ask it (DESIGN 15).

freshness.description: The declared honest freshness, e.g. "60s". For watched facts this is the reconcile interval (DESIGN 30). The unit is part of the value: a bare "60" would be read as seconds by one consumer and milliseconds by another, and staleness verdicts hang off this number.

answer.description: The facts that belong on a row (DESIGN 26).

ceiling.description: A scope error made visible, not a transport limit to paginate around (DESIGN 19).

discovers.description: Present where this collection produces estate-membership candidates: its universe and blind spots, stated by the collector that knows its interface (DESIGN 22).

names.description: Every name family this collection publishes, by stability class. A join runs on stable only (DESIGN 16, 19).

reference_residue.description: Reference opinion keys this collection's rule table does NOT carry under that name, each with the reason. Required wherever the port's table is smaller than the rulebook it was written from, and checked deny-by-default against the reference — which is DESIGN 17's third property, the one that makes the named-evaluator seam a mechanism rather than an escape hatch: a reader asking why a rule table is smaller than a rulebook gets an answer from the declaration instead of inferring one from silence. Added 2026-08-23, the day an audit found that property asserted in DESIGN, in a code comment and in a test comment, and implemented nowhere — a present-tense claim naming no guard, false on the day it was written. Two dispositions matter and both are stated in the reason: a key the table genuinely does not decide, and a key decided under a DIFFERENT name. The second is not cosmetic: a rule key is part of a finding's identity and renaming one resets a lifecycle, so a rename that nothing records is a lifecycle reset nobody can find.

reason.description: Why this table does not carry it: the fact it would need and nothing emits, the condition the vocabulary cannot express, or the key it is decided under instead.

rules.description: This collection's self-evident opinions, kept as data so they can be read before they run. A collector this repository does not ship brings its own rules the same way it brings its own facts, which is the whole of what makes a plugin able to say why one of its facts is alarming (DESIGN appendix C, ruled 2026-08-20).

discriminator.description: The facts that distinguish parallel instances. Absent asserts at-most-singular, and a second instance is an error (DESIGN 13).

confirmed_by.description: The assertion type that confirms this relation from the far end. Required where inverse_observable is true; pairing carries a maximum age spread derived from the tighter collection's declared freshness (DESIGN 19).

allOf.description: carries_facts is a promise the facts map must keep in both directions: true with no facts declares semantics nobody stated, false with facts ships semantics nobody promised.

redactions.description: Payload paths whose values are not served verbatim, each with what it reveals. The secret class is withheld entirely; the others are substituted for a public corpus (DESIGN 21).

redaction_exemption.description: The reviewed statement that this source has no credential surface. Load-bearing prose: carried verbatim, never paraphrased.

mutations.description: Declared and never executed by anything defined in the design (DESIGN 19, 34).

verbs.description: The request-shaped verbs this collection serves, each with its own byte and time bounds (DESIGN 18/19): they run single-flight per collector, and a response that hits its bound says so on the payload — a truncated document marked truncated is still evidence; an unmarked one is a lie about the system. A collection without this member serves collect alone, and the verbs are refused unsupported.

hide_groups.description: Groups of rows a surface may hide by default, in the order they are offered. Optional: a collection declaring none shows every row, which is the safe direction.

collection.$comment: Exactly one, never neither and never both (DESIGN 19): declaring neither is a build failure, and an exemption asserting no credential surface beside a declared redaction list is two rulings contradicting each other in one document.

sentence.description: What one of the two consumers renders (DESIGN 28). Never a label.

values.description: Closed members, where type is enum.

bound.description: The fact naming this gauge's bound, where one exists (DESIGN 27).

denominator.description: The fact this percentage is over (DESIGN 27).

rate_companion.description: The derived windowed gauge published beside this counter (DESIGN 12).

from.description: Extraction path into the evidence payload; what makes the digest checkable (DESIGN 24).

discloses.description: Required, with no default: assume nothing and a forgotten serial is published; assume identity and the corpus is scrubbed into uselessness (DESIGN 21).

allOf.description: An enum without its members is an open set a renderer must guess at; members on any other type are a vocabulary nothing will ever check a value against.
labels is a boolean's pair of display words (DESIGN 27); on any other type the pair is dead weight a renderer might wrongly trust.
Law 4: a derived fact names the facts it consumed — a derivation with no stated inputs cannot be re-checked.
A percentage with no denominator is a number pretending to be an answer (DESIGN 27, 28).

condition.description: One test over one collection's declared facts. The set is CLOSED and small on purpose: a rule table is opinions kept as data, reviewable before it runs, and an expression language that could grow would become a plugin-supplied evaluator by increments — unbounded, and third-party code in the judging path. Every leaf names a fact, and a fact a rule names must be declared by the same collection (DESIGN 17, acceptance item 7).

oneOf.description: Whether the fact has a value at all. Present is NOT truthiness: zero, false and the empty string are readings, and a rule that treated them as absence would be the null-fact family arriving in the judging layer.
For list facts: whether the list has members. Separate from `present` because an empty list is a reading and a missing list is not.

rule.description: One self-evident opinion, as DATA. Self-evident is not a preference here, it is what a collector can know: intent never reaches a host, so a rule that travels with a declaration cannot be intent-relative and this member holds no other kind. Intent-relative opinions are the hub's, from intent (DESIGN 17). A rule carries EXACTLY one of `when` and `evaluator`: both would be two answers to one question with no rule for which wins, and neither is a rule that fires on nothing.

key.description: Stable, and part of a finding's identity — renaming one resets a lifecycle, so it is versioned like a fact name rather than edited freely.

grounds.description: Where the judgement comes from, and the distinction is load-bearing rather than decorative. `interface` means the system itself declares the fault — systemd says `failed`, ZFS says `DEGRADED` — and no number of ours is involved. `threshold` means the number IS ours: 98% full and three days to expiry encode a risk appetite, a workload and a renewal lead time that vary by host and by owner. A surface that rendered both identically would present our opinion as the machine's (DESIGN 17).

sentence.description: What to say. It states the condition, never the remedy: a rule that told an operator what to do would be this product acting through prose.

cites.description: The declared facts a reader can go and look at. At least one, always: an opinion citing nothing is an assertion, and every name here must be declared by this collection — which is acceptance item 7 at the rule table.

applies_to.description: The object TYPES this rule judges, where a collection publishes rows of more than one shape. Absent means every row, which is the ordinary case. Added 2026-08-23 after a measured defect nothing else catches: resources/workloads publishes slices and workloads in one collection, the reference dispatches on row shape and calls slice_opinions OR workload_opinions and never both, and the port — one rule table per collection with no way to name a shape — fired the workload stall rules on slice rows. That restored the operator report of 2026-08-13 verbatim, a slice at 56.35% listed beneath the container scope at 65.27% that explains it, one stall reported twice with the culprit's name removed the second time; and at warn rather than the info the reference suppresses entirely, so it reached the findings surface and the estate roll-up. Every host under I/O load has -.slice and system.slice above the bar, so it fired routinely rather than in a corner. It clears appendix A's budget by naming a defect it alone catches: a collection whose rows have two shapes cannot otherwise be judged correctly by a table addressed to the collection.

evaluator.description: Names an in-tree evaluator that decides this rule, INSTEAD of a `when`. Ruled 2026-08-23 (DESIGN 17): roughly a fifth of opinions need real code — arithmetic with unit rendering, set algebra across list facts, a map indexed by another fact's own name — and the condition vocabulary was deliberately not widened to reach them, because appendix A's budget asks a new member to delete one or name a defect it alone catches, and two rules is thin ground for either. The row keeps every other member, so the opinion stays DECLARED and only the test is code: a reader asking why a rule table is smaller than a rulebook gets an answer from the declaration instead of inferring one from silence. The set is CLOSED and reviewed like a vocabulary — a declaration NAMES an evaluator and cannot ship one, which is the line that keeps third-party code out of the judging path. The price, stated where it bites: a collector this repository does not ship can express the four fifths and cannot express these. A third case reopens the decision, because a steady trickle would mean the vocabulary is wrong.

hide_group.description: One group of rows a surface may hide by default, as DATA. Which rows are ordinarily uninteresting is the PRODUCER's judgement — a renderer deciding it would be a copy of the producer's knowledge (DESIGN 27), which is what the shipping UI's hand-kept table of predicates was. `when` is the same condition vocabulary the rule tables use, so there is one condition language and not two that drift. A row the rulebook called CRITICAL is never suppressed whatever this matches, and that exemption is enforced by the surface rather than restated in every group here: 'the default view never swallows a failure' is the promise the whole mechanism rests on, and a promise each group had to remember is one an added group will forget.

key.description: Stable identifier for the group, used to key the control that reveals it. Not shown to a reader.

label.description: What the chip says. The count beside it answers what this group HOLDS, never what is currently hidden, so it does not change when the chip is pressed.

when.description: Which rows this group holds. A condition that cannot be evaluated leaves rows VISIBLE: the failure mode of a missing group is a longer page, and of a broken one hiding rows anyway is a suppressed fault.
